slides.title: How Should I Pick a Foundation Model for My Robot? In Favor of a Community Evaluation Framework for Social Robots
slides.tldr: EVALUATION FRAMEWORK FOR SOCIAL ROBOT FOUNDATION MODELS
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a three-tiered evaluation funnel and five key dimensions to help researchers select foundation models for social robots, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A proposed three-tiered evaluation framework to help researchers select foundation models for social robots.
card.key_idea: A funnel paradigm filtering models through curated static benchmarks (T1), simulated LLM-based interactions (T2), and robot-specific hardware evaluations (T3) across five key social dimensions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a representative case study with the Haru robot, mapping existing benchmarks to a proposed coverage map.
card.limitation: T3 remains robot-specific and costly; multimodal interaction and the boundary between simulation and live user studies are unresolved.

slides.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR FORECASTING SOCIAL-WORLD EVOLUTION
slides.highlight: SocietyBench evaluates the ability of LLM agents to forecast social events using counterfactual timelines, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: SocietyBench evaluates LLM forecasting of real social events using anonymized, counterfactual timelines to prevent memorization.
card.key_idea: Real events are transformed into counterfactual worlds via entity substitution and date shifting, then scored on probability calibration and temporal accuracy across factual and opinion layers.
card.evaluation: Six frontier LLMs, three agent frameworks, and two heuristics were tested on five heterogeneous events. GPT-5.5 performed best, scoring 75.0/100.
card.limitation: High per-event score variance (up to 21.4 points) makes single-event evaluations unreliable for comparing model performance.

slides.title: TRIBE: Predicting Team Performance via Communication Behavior Ensembles
slides.tldr: PREDICTING TEAM PERFORMANCE VIA COMMUNICATION PATTERNS
slides.highlight: TRIBE uses communication patterns to categorize team behavioral dynamics and predict performance, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception of hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: TRIBE predicts team performance by clustering communication patterns, enabling interventions as early as 10% task completion.
card.key_idea: A domain-independent pipeline using topic modeling (NMF/LDA) and clustering (GMM/K-means) to categorize teams into performance-predictive 'behavioral tribes' based on interaction transcripts.
card.evaluation: Tested on four diverse datasets (Minecraft, DELI, GAP). Adjusted R² reached 44.3% in Study 4; results were statistically significant for three datasets.
card.limitation: Predictive strength depends on the task structure's degree of behavioral freedom; finite-answer tasks show limited behavioral variation.

slides.title: Designing Social Robots for Inclusive Child Wellbeing Assessment: Insights from Communities Supporting Developmental Language Disorder and Forced Migration
slides.tldr: INCLUSIVE SOCIAL ROBOTS FOR CHILD WELLBEING ASSESSMENT
slides.highlight: This research provides design recommendations for using social robots to assess the wellbeing of children with communication barriers, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Stakeholder insights for designing inclusive social robot interactions to assess wellbeing in children with communication barriers.
card.key_idea: Used design probes and focus groups with parents and professionals to derive ethical, inclusive recommendations for robot-mediated wellbeing assessments for children with DLD and forced migration backgrounds.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of focus group discussions with 14 stakeholders (parents and professionals) across two specific vulnerable child populations.
card.limitation: The study is a qualitative, participatory design phase; it does not yet test the robot interactions with children directly.

slides.title: Is Inter-Seed Cross-Play Enough? Evaluating the Robustness of Zero-Shot Coordination Algorithms to Implementation Details
slides.tldr: ROBUSTNESS EVALUATION OF ZERO-SHOT COORDINATION
slides.highlight: This work evaluates the robustness of zero-shot coordination (ZSC) algorithms to implementation details, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of creating AI teammates that can coordinate with partners at test time.

card.one_liner: Inter-seed cross-play is a reliable proxy for evaluating zero-shot coordination robustness across different implementations.
card.key_idea: Introduces cross-implementation cross-play (XIXP), varying PPO implementation details (e.g., learning rate, weight initialization) to test if ZSC algorithms remain robust beyond random seed variations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Other-Play using IPPO in the Yokai environment; compared within-implementation (WIXP) and cross-implementation (XIXP) scores across 11 competent implementations.
card.limitation: Analysis is restricted to one environment (Yokai), one base algorithm (IPPO), and one ZSC algorithm (Other-Play).

slides.title: Humanoid Companion Robot Market Projected to Reach US$1.1bn by 2030
slides.tldr: GROWTH IN HUMANOID COMPANION ROBOT MARKET
slides.highlight: The increasing demand for caregiving and emotional support is driving the humanoid companion robot market. This trend aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Dobot Launches Full-Scenario Embodied Humanoid Robot
slides.tldr: NEW MULTI-FUNCTIONAL EMBODIED HUMANOID ROBOT
slides.highlight: The launch of a multi-functional humanoid robot for daily and professional needs is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: When AI Joins the Team! A Model of How AI Adoption Relates To Social Patterns in Software Engineering Teams
slides.tldr: AI ADOPTION AND TEAM SOCIAL DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research examines how AI adoption affects social patterns and communication quality in software teams, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AI adoption reduces community smells through different mechanisms depending on whether work involves specialization or coordination.
card.key_idea: Using TMS theory and PLS-SEM, the study models AI adoption's impact on community smells via two paths: indirectly through peer interaction (specialization) and directly via communication quality (coordination).
card.evaluation: Validated via expert surveys, EFA, and PLS-SEM on survey data from 152 software professionals using AI tools.
card.limitation: The study relies on developers' perceptions of community smells rather than objective technical metrics.

slides.title: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Reasoning Models: Robustness over Reasoning
slides.tldr: REASONING MODELS SHOW INCREASED ROBUSTNESS IN THEORY OF MIND TASKS
slides.highlight: This research examines how reasoning-oriented LLMs exhibit increased robustness to prompt variations in Theory of Mind tasks, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on inferring partner intent via theory of mind.

card.one_liner: Reasoning models improve Theory of Mind performance primarily through increased robustness rather than new cognitive abilities.
card.key_idea: The authors analyze reasoning-oriented LLMs using psychological tests and prompt perturbations, suggesting that 'thinking' tokens stabilize the path to correct answers already possible for base models.
card.evaluation: Evaluated GPT-5, Claude, R1, and Grok-3-mini using Sally-Anne tests, Strange Stories, and modified prompts. Results show high accuracy and improved stability over non-reasoning counterparts.
card.limitation: Behavioral analysis lacks causal identification of RLVR training effects; some failures suggest a lack of mental visual representation.

slides.authors: Ian B. de Haan et al.

slides.title: Deep Learning for Real-Time Sound Order Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME SOUND ORDER RECOGNITION FOR HRI
slides.highlight: This research proposes a deep learning framework to recognize the temporal order of overlapping sounds, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A deep learning framework for real-time recognition of the temporal order of overlapping non-verbal sounds.
card.key_idea: A multi-branch CNN processing Mel spectrograms, MFCCs, and STFT features, utilizing an attention-based fusion mechanism to identify sound sequences.
card.evaluation: Tested on synthetic overlaps (same/varied amplitude, unseen sounds); achieved 99% accuracy for balanced overlaps and 74% for unseen data.
card.limitation: Experiments relied on carefully controlled synthetic overlaps, raising concerns regarding ecological validity in real-room environments.

slides.title: Claude Code Update Enables Autonomous AI Session Communication
slides.tldr: AUTONOMOUS MULTI-AGENT COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: The update allows AI sessions to communicate autonomously, providing a relevant example of multi-agent collaboration for MIMIC's societal-scale simulations.

slides.title: Toward Resilient Human-AI Collaboration: A Lifecycle Taxonomy of Sociotechnical Risks and Cascading Failures
slides.tldr: SOCIOTECHNICAL RISK TAXONOMY FOR HUMAN-AI COLLABORATION
slides.highlight: This work identifies recurring risk clusters and cascading failures in human-AI collaboration, providing a framework for understanding the sociotechnical dynamics relevant to HyECHO's focus on hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: A lifecycle taxonomy identifying six recurring sociotechnical risk clusters that undermine resilient human-AI collaboration across diverse professional domains.
card.key_idea: Synthesizes risks into a four-stage lifecycle (task allocation, interaction, feedback, adoption) and six cross-domain clusters: Trust Miscalibration, Cognitive Burden, Accountability Gap, Capability Erosion, Goal Misalignment, and Technostress.
card.evaluation: Conceptual synthesis of existing literature across five domains (healthcare, journalism, education, management, defense); no new empirical datasets or baselines provided.
card.limitation: The work is a conceptual framework and taxonomy; it lacks empirical validation and quantitative testing of the proposed interaction model.

slides.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation
slides.tldr: LEARNING HUMAN-LIKE ROBOT MOTION FROM HANDWRITING DEMONSTRATIONS
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for learning human-like robot motion through handwriting demonstrations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A framework for learning human-like robot handwriting using an extended GMM+GMR approach with force and timing.
card.key_idea: Extends GMM+GMR by incorporating contact force and normalized time dimensions and implementing a segment-detection step to handle non-continuous, multi-stroke trajectories.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via a user study (21 participants) on 52 characters; generated trajectories achieved a mean human-likeness score of 71.50/100.
card.limitation: Evaluations used a simulated robot rather than physical hardware; sample sizes were small and pen orientation was not recorded.

slides.title: Vibe Compiler: A Research-Logic Synthesis Tool That Runs without Prompt Engineering
slides.tldr: ENHANCING METACOGNITION FOR HUMAN AGENCY
slides.highlight: The Vibe Compiler uses a Synthesis-Analysis Reciprocity Model to stimulate human metacognition by prompting researchers to fill logical gaps, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Vibe Compiler transforms vague research ideas into rigorous logic by stimulating human metacognition through AI-detected structural gaps.
card.key_idea: A Synthesis–Analysis Reciprocity Model using a 16-parameter paper ontology to identify logical gaps, prompting researchers with reflective questions instead of providing autonomous AI solutions.
card.evaluation: Prototype built on NotebookLM and Gemini; verified via execution logs that it detects null slots and constructs research logic (e.g., this paper).
card.limitation: Lacks quantitative data on whether structural gaps statistically improve evaluative judgement; not designed for complete novices.

slides.title: D-CLOT: Double Closed Loop Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Action Segmentation
slides.tldr: UNSUPERVISED ACTION SEGMENTATION VIA DOUBLE CLOSED LOOP OPTIMAL TRANSPORT
slides.highlight: This work introduces a double closed loop optimal transport framework to resolve representation-prototype inconsistency in unsupervised action segmentation, aligning with MOSAIC's use of Optimal Transport for human-AI intent alignment.

card.one_liner: D-CLOT improves unsupervised action segmentation by periodically re-aligning action prototypes with refined frame representations.
card.key_idea: Extends CLOT with a graph-constrained regularizer to stabilize frame geometry and an action-embedding refinement step using either k-means or assignment-aware OT barycenters.
card.evaluation: Tested on five benchmarks (YTII, FS, DA, BF, and Assembly101) using F1 and mIoU; results show significant gains over CLOT.

slides.title: PromptShield Home: Ambient Multimodal Prompt Injection Defense for Smart-Home Agents
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL PROMPT INJECTION DEFENSE FOR SMART HOMES
slides.highlight: This work addresses addressee ambiguity and multimodal prompt injection in smart-home agents, contributing to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: PromptShield-Home benchmarks multimodal prompt injection in smart homes, finding MLLMs over-refuse while traditional detectors over-execute.
card.key_idea: A three-layer framework comparing traditional detectors (L0), single MLLMs (L1), and multi-agent mediation (L2) to evaluate safety and utility in ambient smart-home scenarios.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 19 pilot scenarios using unsafe-execution and safe-completion rates. Results show an oracle combining L0 and vision-MLLM reaches 94.1% accuracy.
card.limitation: Small benchmark size (N=19), lack of a trained router, and high VRAM requirements for the 30B vision model.

slides.title: Human Centric Embodied Intelligence for Soft Wearable Robotics
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTRIC EMBODIED INTELLIGENCE FOR SOFT WEARABLES
slides.highlight: This review introduces the PCAA framework to shift soft wearable robotics toward human-centric embodied intelligence, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A review proposing the PCAA framework to shift soft wearable robotics toward human-centric embodied intelligence.
card.key_idea: The Perception-Cognition-Actuation-Augmentation (PCAA) framework prioritizes sensing and cognition over actuators to enable adaptive, personalized human-robot coupling.

slides.title: Accelerating Human-Aware Robot Trajectory Generation via Diffusion and Consistency Distillation
slides.tldr: FAST HUMAN-AWARE TRAJECTORY GENERATION
slides.highlight: This work presents a framework for generating collision-aware robot manipulator trajectories using diffusion models and consistency distillation. It is relevant to RwB for improving safety and smoothness in human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Accelerates human-aware robot trajectory generation using consistency distillation and jerk regularization for smoother, faster motion planning.
card.key_idea: A conditional diffusion model trained on RRT/RRT* data, distilled into a consistency model for few-step sampling, featuring constraint-guided inference and joint-weighted jerk regularization.
card.evaluation: Simulated UR5 manipulator (500 test scenes); measured success rate, inference time, and jerk. Consistency model generated 150 candidates in <100ms with high success rates.
card.limitation: Evaluated only in simulation using a UR5 manipulator; real-world physical validation is not clearly stated.

slides.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning
slides.tldr: TEST-TIME SELF-CORRECTION FOR LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: This work proposes a verifier-free framework that uses iterative self-critique and self-correction to refine reasoning rollouts at test time. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that self-monitor and self-correct via meta-cognition to adapt during execution.

card.one_liner: Improves LLM reasoning by iteratively refining multiple sampled trajectories through self-critique and correction before majority voting.
card.key_idea: A training-free, verifier-free framework combining breadth (N independent rollouts) and depth (D rounds of self-critique and self-correction) to repair reasoning errors without external reward models.
card.evaluation: Tested on AIME24, AIME25, AMC, OlympiadBench, and MATH500 across four open-weight models; consistently outperformed greedy, majority voting, and verifier-based baselines.
card.limitation: Higher inference cost due to multiple forward passes and dependence on the base model's intrinsic ability to accurately self-critique.

slides.title: The Calibration Floor: Format Repair Can Masquerade as Self-Correction at Small-to-Mid Scale
slides.tldr: FORMAT REPAIR MASKING SELF-CORRECTION
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that perceived self-correction in language models often results from format repair rather than reasoning changes, which is critical for ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognitive self-monitoring and correction.

card.one_liner: Apparent LLM self-correction gains are often just format repairs masquerading as reasoning improvements.
card.key_idea: Decomposes self-correction accuracy into a 'content margin' (both answers parseable) and 'format margins' (parseability changes), using grammar-constrained decoding to causally isolate reasoning effects.
card.evaluation: Tested across Qwen3.5 (0.8B-9B), Gemma-4-12B, and frontier models (Hy3, Nemotron-3-Ultra) on GSM8K, MMLU, and MATH using a calibration-floor instrument.
card.limitation: Frontier model testing was lower-powered due to API rate limits and missing logprobs; MATH grading relied on string normalization.

slides.title: Mimir: A Neuro-Symbolic Memory System with Dynamic Grounding for Embodied Agents in Interactive Environments
slides.tldr: NEURO-SYMBOLIC MEMORY FOR EMBODIED AGENTS
slides.highlight: Mimir introduces a neuro-symbolic memory system that separates world and task memory to improve long-horizon embodied task success. This aligns with MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic and agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Mimir improves long-horizon embodied tasks by separating world belief from task progress via dynamic grounding.
card.key_idea: A neuro-symbolic system using world memory (object states/locations) and task memory (goal agenda/progress), linked by a grounding module that binds active goals to recalled evidence.
card.evaluation: Tested on EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat across 13 backbones; showed average success rate gains of 23.0% and 86.0% SR on EB-Habitat Long-horizon.
card.limitation: Cannot resolve targets that are not identifiable from inputs due to ambiguous descriptions or severe occlusion.

slides.title: Certifying Collective Reasoning in Multi-Agent Systems via Koopman Spectral Analysis
slides.tldr: SPECTRAL CERTIFICATION OF MULTI-AGENT REASONING
slides.highlight: This work provides a framework to certify convergence and explainability in multi-agent collectives, supporting the MOSAIC goal of aligning human-AI intent through principled analysis of interaction dynamics.

card.one_liner: Certifies multi-agent LLM collective reasoning by analyzing the spectrum of a linear Koopman transfer operator.
card.key_idea: Lifts nonlinear agent interaction traces into a linear Koopman space via EDMD, using the sub-dominant eigenvalue to compute convergence deadlines and eigenvectors for faction attribution.
card.evaluation: Validated on an attention-consensus model across 24 configurations; showed 0.93 log-log correlation for deadlines and 99.7% fidelity for spectral message compression.
card.limitation: The theoretical guarantees currently rely on a spectral dominance assumption (constant C=1) and were validated on a reference model.
